title.en: tend to · will / would for habits · be always + -ing (annoying habits) · keep (on) + -ing

summary.es: tend to · will / would for habits · be always + -ing (annoying habits) · keep (on) + -ing

explanation.es:
Hablar de tendencias

tend to + verboI tend to get up late at weekends. (suelo)
will (hábito típico, característico)She'll spend hours reading if you let her.
would (hábito pasado)As a child I would hide under the table.
keep (on) + -ingHe keeps forgetting his keys. (no para de)

Hábitos que molestan: always + continuo

Con always / constantly / forever el presente o el pasado continuo expresa irritación:

You're always leaving your socks on the floor! (¡siempre dejas…!)
She was constantly complaining about her job.
Compara: He always arrives on time (dato neutro) / He's always arriving late! (queja). El acento va en always.
«Suelo» en presente nunca es use to: ✗ I use to go → ✓ I usually go / I tend to go. Would no sirve para estados del pasado: ✗ I would have a dog → ✓ I used to have a dog.

examples.en: I tend to eat too much when I'm stressed.
examples.es: Suelo comer demasiado cuando estoy estresado.

examples.en: You're always interrupting me! Let me finish.
examples.es: ¡Siempre me estás interrumpiendo! Déjame terminar.

examples.en: My computer keeps crashing . I need a new one.
examples.es: Mi ordenador no para de colgarse. Necesito uno nuevo.

examples.en: When I was little, my dad would read me a story every night.
examples.es: De pequeño, mi padre me leía un cuento todas las noches.

examples.en: She tends to leave everything until the last minute.
examples.es: Suele dejarlo todo para el último momento.

examples.en: He's forever losing his phone.
examples.es: Se pasa la vida perdiendo el móvil.

title.en: past perfect simple vs continuous · narrative linkers: as soon as, no sooner, by the time, eventually

summary.es: past perfect simple vs continuous · narrative linkers: as soon as, no sooner, by the time, eventually

explanation.es:
Pasado perfecto continuo

had been + -ing. Actividad que duraba hasta un momento del pasado (o justo antes). Pone el foco en la duración o en la causa de algo visible:

The ground was wet. It had been raining all night.
She was exhausted because she had been working for twelve hours.
We had been walking for an hour when we realised we were lost.
Past perfect simplePast perfect continuous
acción terminada, resultado, cantidadactividad, duración
She had written three chapters.She had been writing since dawn.

Conectores narrativos

As soon as he arrived, …en cuanto llegó
By the time we got there, the shop had closed.para cuando llegamos
Eventually, they found the way.al final (tras mucho tiempo)
Meanwhile, …mientras tanto
No sooner had I sat down than the phone rang.nada más sentarme (formal, con inversión)
Los verbos de estado no van en continuo: ✗ I had been knowing her → ✓ I had known her for years.

examples.en: Her eyes were red. She had been crying.
examples.es: Tenía los ojos rojos. Había estado llorando.

examples.en: We had been waiting for two hours when the bus finally came.
examples.es: Llevábamos dos horas esperando cuando por fin llegó el autobús.

examples.en: By the time I got home, they had eaten all the cake.
examples.es: Para cuando llegué a casa, se habían comido todo el pastel.

examples.en: No sooner had we left than it started to rain.
examples.es: Nada más salir, empezó a llover.

examples.en: He had been driving for hours and he was exhausted.
examples.es: Llevaba horas conduciendo y estaba agotado.

examples.en: As soon as she opened the door, she knew something was wrong.
examples.es: En cuanto abrió la puerta, supo que algo iba mal.

title.en: future continuous: will be + -ing · future perfect: will have + participle · be about to, be due to, be bound to, be on the point of

summary.es: future continuous: will be + -ing · future perfect: will have + participle · be about to, be due to, be bound to, be on the point of

explanation.es:
Futuro continuo

will be + -ing: algo que estará en curso en un momento futuro; también planes que siguen su curso normal:

This time tomorrow I'll be lying on a beach. (estaré tumbado)
Will you be using the car tonight? (pregunta educada por los planes)

Futuro perfecto

will have + participio: algo que ya habrá terminado antes de un momento futuro, normalmente con by:

By 2030, they will have finished the new airport.
By the time you arrive, I'll have cooked dinner.

Otras expresiones de futuro

be about to + verboThe film is about to start. (está a punto de)
be on the point of + -ingI was on the point of leaving when she called.
be due to + verboThe train is due to arrive at 6. (está previsto)
be bound to + verboIt's bound to rain. (seguro que…)
be likely / unlikely toPrices are likely to rise.
Tras by the time, when, as soon as, until, presente aunque hable del futuro: ✗ by the time you will arrive → ✓ by the time you arrive.

examples.en: Don't call at nine. We'll be having dinner then.
examples.es: No llames a las nueve. Estaremos cenando.

examples.en: By the end of the year, I'll have saved enough money for the trip.
examples.es: Para final de año, habré ahorrado suficiente dinero para el viaje.

examples.en: Hurry up! The train is about to leave.
examples.es: ¡Date prisa! El tren está a punto de salir.

examples.en: She's worked so hard. She's bound to pass.
examples.es: Ha trabajado muchísimo. Seguro que aprueba.

examples.en: By next June I will have lived here for ten years.
examples.es: En junio hará diez años que vivo aquí.

examples.en: Will you be going to the meeting tomorrow?
examples.es: ¿Vas a ir a la reunión de mañana?

title.en: must have / might have / can't have + participle · should have / ought to have · needn't have / didn't need to · could have

summary.es: must have / might have / can't have + participle · should have / ought to have · needn't have / didn't need to · could have

explanation.es:
Deducir sobre el pasado

casi seguro que símust have + participioThe streets are wet. It must have rained.
posiblemight / may / could haveShe might have missed the bus.
casi seguro que nocan't / couldn't haveHe can't have seen us. He didn't say hello.

Criticar y lamentar

should have / ought to havelo correcto habría sido (no se hizo)You should have told me!
shouldn't havese hizo, y fue un errorI shouldn't have eaten so much.
could haveposibilidad no aprovechada; reprocheYou could have hurt yourself! You could have called.

needn't have / didn't need to

I needn't have brought an umbrella. (lo traje y no hacía falta)
I didn't need to bring an umbrella. (no hacía falta; normalmente no lo traje)
En la conversación suenan reducidos: should've, must've, could've /ʃʊdəv/. Por eso los nativos a veces escriben mal «should of». ✗ must had → ✓ must have + participio. Fíjate: «debió de llover» = it must have rained; «debería haber llamado» = I should have called.

examples.en: The lights are off. They must have gone to bed.
examples.es: Las luces están apagadas. Deben de haberse ido a la cama.

examples.en: He can't have sent the letter. It's still here.
examples.es: No puede haber enviado la carta. Sigue aquí.

examples.en: You should have told me it was a formal party!
examples.es: ¡Me deberías haber dicho que era una fiesta formal!

examples.en: I needn't have cooked so much. Nobody was hungry.
examples.es: No hacía falta que cocinara tanto. Nadie tenía hambre.

examples.en: We should have booked a table.
examples.es: Deberíamos haber reservado mesa.

examples.en: They must have got lost on the way.
examples.es: Se deben de haber perdido por el camino.

title.en: mixed conditionals · unless, provided (that), as long as, suppose, otherwise, even if · inverted conditionals (Should you…, Had I known…)
title.es: Si las cosas hubieran sido distintas

summary.es: mixed conditionals · unless, provided (that), as long as, suppose, otherwise, even if · inverted conditionals (Should you…, Had I known…)

explanation.es:
Condicionales mixtos

Combinan tiempos distintos en la condición y en el resultado:

Condición pasada → resultado presenteCondición presente → resultado pasado
If I had taken that job, I'd be rich now.If I weren't so shy, I'd have spoken to her.
(if + past perfect, would + verbo)(if + past simple, would have + participio)

Alternativas a if

unlessa menos queI won't go unless you come.
provided / providing (that), as long assiempre queYou can borrow it as long as you're careful.
suppose / supposing¿y si…?, supongamos queSuppose you lost your job, what would you do?
even ifaunque (incluso si)I'll go even if it rains.
otherwisesi no, de lo contrarioHurry, otherwise we'll be late.

Condicionales con inversión (formal)

Should you need help, call me. (= If you should need…)
Had I known, I would have come. (= If I had known…)
Were I in your position, I'd resign. (= If I were…)
✗ Unless you don't hurry → ✓ Unless you hurry (unless ya es negativo). even if ≠ even though: even though = aunque (es un hecho).

examples.en: If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.
examples.es: Si hubiera estudiado Medicina, ahora sería médico.

examples.en: If she weren't so stubborn, she would have apologised.
examples.es: Si no fuera tan terca, se habría disculpado.

examples.en: I'll lend you the money provided you pay me back next week.
examples.es: Te presto el dinero siempre que me lo devuelvas la semana que viene.

examples.en: Had I known about the problem, I would have helped.
examples.es: De haber sabido lo del problema, habría ayudado.

examples.en: If I hadn't missed that train, we would never have met.
examples.es: Si no hubiera perdido aquel tren, nunca nos habríamos conocido.

examples.en: Take a map, otherwise you'll get lost.
examples.es: Llévate un mapa; si no, te perderás.

title.en: wish + would · I'd rather + past · it's (high) time + past · as if / as though

summary.es: wish + would · I'd rather + past · it's (high) time + past · as if / as though

explanation.es:
wish + would

Para quejarse de lo que otra persona hace (o no hace) y nos gustaría que cambiara:

I wish you would stop interrupting me. (ojalá dejaras de…)
I wish it would stop raining.
wish + pasadosituación presente irrealI wish I lived nearer.
wish + past perfectarrepentimiento pasadoI wish I hadn't gone.
wish + wouldqueja, deseo de cambio de otroI wish he would listen.
No se usa wish + would con uno mismo: ✗ I wish I would… → ✓ I wish I could… Para deseos posibles de futuro se usa hope: I hope you pass (✗ I wish you pass).

I'd rather · It's time · as if

I'd rather + forma base (yo)I'd rather stay in.
I'd rather + otra persona + pasadoI'd rather you didn't smoke here. (preferiría que no fumaras)
It's (high) time + sujeto + pasadoIt's time we went home. It's high time you found a job.
as if / as though + pasado (irreal)He talks as if he knew everything.
Todas estas estructuras usan el pasado con valor irreal, igual que el español usa el imperfecto de subjuntivo: «preferiría que no fumaras», «ya es hora de que nos fuéramos».

examples.en: I wish my neighbours wouldn't make so much noise.
examples.es: Ojalá mis vecinos no hicieran tanto ruido.

examples.en: It's time we went home. It's very late.
examples.es: Ya es hora de irnos a casa. Es muy tarde.

examples.en: I'd rather you didn't tell anyone about this.
examples.es: Preferiría que no se lo contaras a nadie.

examples.en: He spends money as if he were a millionaire.
examples.es: Gasta dinero como si fuera millonario.

examples.en: I wish you would listen to me for once.
examples.es: Ojalá me escucharas por una vez.

examples.en: It's high time the government did something.
examples.es: Ya va siendo hora de que el gobierno haga algo.

title.en: impersonal passive: It is said that… / He is said to… · passive with two objects · have / get something done · be supposed to

summary.es: impersonal passive: It is said that… / He is said to… · passive with two objects · have / get something done · be supposed to

explanation.es:
Pasiva impersonal

Típica de las noticias, para opiniones y rumores sin decir quién los dice:

It + pasiva + thatSujeto + pasiva + to-infinitivo
It is said that he is very rich.He is said to be very rich.
It is believed that the thief escaped.The thief is believed to have escaped.
It is expected that prices will rise.Prices are expected to rise.
Si lo dicho es anterior al momento en que se dice, usa el infinitivo perfecto: She is thought to have left the country (se cree que se ha ido). Verbos típicos: say, believe, think, know, report, expect, consider, estimate, allege.

Pasiva con dos objetos

They gave her a prize. → She was given a prize. (lo más natural en inglés)
They sent me the documents. → I was sent the documents.

Causativa y be supposed to

have / get + objeto + participioI'm having my car repaired. She got her bag stolen. (le robaron)
be supposed toYou're supposed to wear a helmet. (se supone que; deberías) · The film is supposed to be good. (dicen que)
El español dice «se dice / se cree»; el inglés no usa reflexivo: ✗ It says that he is rich (= el texto dice) → ✓ It is said that he is rich.

examples.en: It is said that the castle is haunted.
examples.es: Se dice que el castillo está encantado.

examples.en: The president is believed to have left the country last night.
examples.es: Se cree que el presidente salió del país anoche.

examples.en: I was given a free ticket for the concert.
examples.es: Me regalaron una entrada para el concierto.

examples.en: You're supposed to switch off your phone in the theatre.
examples.es: Se supone que hay que apagar el móvil en el teatro.

examples.en: The painting is thought to be worth millions.
examples.es: Se cree que el cuadro vale millones.

examples.en: We are having our kitchen redecorated.
examples.es: Nos están reformando la cocina.

title.en: reporting verbs + to / + -ing / + that / + object + to · accuse of, blame for, apologise for, insist on

summary.es: reporting verbs + to / + -ing / + that / + object + to · accuse of, blame for, apologise for, insist on

explanation.es:
Patrones de los verbos de habla

PatrónVerbosEjemplo
+ to + verboagree, offer, promise, refuse, threaten, claimHe refused to help.
+ objeto + toadvise, persuade, encourage, remind, urge, warn, invite, tell, askShe persuaded me to stay.
+ -ingadmit, deny, suggest, recommend, regretHe denied stealing the money.
+ preposición + -ingapologise for, insist on, accuse sb of, blame sb for, congratulate sb on, thank sb forThey accused him of lying.
+ that + fraseexplain, complain, announce, admit, deny, suggest, insist, promiseShe explained that the shop was closed.
suggest nunca lleva objeto + to: ✗ He suggested me to go → ✓ He suggested going / He suggested that I (should) go. Igual con recommend.
Estos verbos resumen mejor que say la intención de lo dicho. «"Fui yo", dijo» → He admitted doing it. «"Te lo devuelvo mañana"» → She promised to give it back.

examples.en: He denied breaking the window.
examples.es: Negó haber roto la ventana.

examples.en: She offered to drive me to the station.
examples.es: Se ofreció a llevarme a la estación.

examples.en: My doctor advised me to do more exercise.
examples.es: Mi médico me aconsejó hacer más ejercicio.

examples.en: They accused him of stealing the money.
examples.es: Le acusaron de robar el dinero.

examples.en: She reminded me to buy some milk.
examples.es: Me recordó que comprara leche.

examples.en: He insisted on paying for dinner.
examples.es: Insistió en pagar la cena.

title.en: prepositions in relative clauses · quantifiers + of whom / of which · whose, whereby, what · reduced relative clauses

summary.es: prepositions in relative clauses · quantifiers + of whom / of which · whose, whereby, what · reduced relative clauses

explanation.es:
Preposición + relativo

Informal (preposición al final)Formal (preposición delante)
the man (who) I spoke tothe man to whom I spoke
the house (that) I grew up inthe house in which I grew up
Tras preposición: whom (personas) y which (cosas), nunca who ni that: ✗ the man to who / ✗ the house in that.

Cuantificador + of whom / of which

I have three brothers, all of whom live abroad. (todos los cuales)
She bought ten books, most of which were second-hand.
The flats, none of which have a lift, are cheap.

what y oraciones reducidas

what = lo queWhat I need is a holiday.
relativa reducida con -ing (activa)People living in the centre (= who live) pay more.
relativa reducida con participio (pasiva)Houses built before 1900 (= which were built) …
whereby (formal) = por el cual, mediante el cual: a system whereby residents can vote online.

examples.en: She has two sisters, both of whom are doctors.
examples.es: Tiene dos hermanas, las dos médicas.

examples.en: This is the house in which Shakespeare was born.
examples.es: Esta es la casa en la que nació Shakespeare.

examples.en: What surprised me most was his reaction.
examples.es: Lo que más me sorprendió fue su reacción.

examples.en: The people living in this building complain about the noise.
examples.es: La gente que vive en este edificio se queja del ruido.

examples.en: The candidates, none of whom had experience, were nervous.
examples.es: Los candidatos, ninguno de los cuales tenía experiencia, estaban nerviosos.

examples.en: Most of the houses built after the war are small.
examples.es: La mayoría de las casas construidas después de la guerra son pequeñas.

title.en: present participle clauses (-ing) · perfect participle (having + participle) · past participle clauses · not + participle

summary.es: present participle clauses (-ing) · perfect participle (having + participle) · past participle clauses · not + participle

explanation.es:
¿Qué son?

Frases sin sujeto ni verbo conjugado que sustituyen a una oración con when, because, after, if… Son típicas de la lengua escrita:

Oración completaOración de participio
When she opened the door, she saw…Opening the door, she saw…
Because I didn't know what to do, I called…Not knowing what to do, I called…
After he had finished, he left.Having finished, he left.
The book, which was written in 1900, …Written in 1900, the book…

Tres formas

-ing (activo, simultáneo o causa)Feeling tired, I went to bed.
having + participio (anterior)Having lived in Japan, she speaks Japanese.
participio (pasivo)Built in 1890, the bridge is still in use.
El sujeto implícito tiene que ser el mismo que el de la oración principal. ✗ Walking down the street, a car hit me (¡el coche iba andando!) → ✓ Walking down the street, I was hit by a car.
Con preposiciones también: On arriving, she called her mother (nada más llegar). After finishing university, he travelled.

examples.en: Having finished his homework, he went out to play.
examples.es: Después de terminar los deberes, salió a jugar.

examples.en: Built in 1889, the Eiffel Tower is the symbol of Paris.
examples.es: Construida en 1889, la Torre Eiffel es el símbolo de París.

examples.en: Not knowing anyone at the party, she left early.
examples.es: Como no conocía a nadie en la fiesta, se fue pronto.

examples.en: On arriving at the airport, we went straight to the hotel.
examples.es: Nada más llegar al aeropuerto, fuimos directos al hotel.

examples.en: Having lived abroad, she understands other cultures.
examples.es: Como ha vivido en el extranjero, entiende otras culturas.

examples.en: Surrounded by mountains, the village is very peaceful.
examples.es: Rodeado de montañas, el pueblo es muy tranquilo.

title.en: cleft sentences: What… is… / It was… that… / All I… · emphatic do / does / did · the thing / the reason / the place… is

summary.es: cleft sentences: What… is… / It was… that… / All I… · emphatic do / does / did · the thing / the reason / the place… is

explanation.es:
Oraciones escindidas (cleft sentences)

Dividen la frase para destacar una parte, como el español «Lo que…es…» / «Fue… quien…»:

NeutraEnfática
I need a holiday.What I need is a holiday.
His attitude annoys me.What annoys me is his attitude.
Tom broke the window.It was Tom who broke the window.
I met her in Paris.It was in Paris that I met her.
I only want to sleep.All I want is to sleep.
We left because of the noise.The reason (why) we left was the noise.

do / does / did enfáticos

En afirmativas, el auxiliar añade énfasis o contraste («sí que…»):

I do like your dress! (¡sí que me gusta!)
She says I never help, but I did help yesterday!
Do sit down. (invitación insistente, educada)
Con What… is + verbo: What I did was (to) call the police. Otros recursos: the thing is…, the problem is…, the point is…, the place where….
✗ That I need is a rest → ✓ What I need is a rest. ✗ It was Tom which broke it → ✓ It was Tom who broke it.

examples.en: What I don't understand is why she left.
examples.es: Lo que no entiendo es por qué se fue.

examples.en: It was my sister who told me the news.
examples.es: Fue mi hermana quien me dio la noticia.

examples.en: I do want to help, but I'm really busy.
examples.es: De verdad que quiero ayudar, pero estoy muy liado.

examples.en: All I want is a quiet weekend.
examples.es: Lo único que quiero es un fin de semana tranquilo.

examples.en: What really annoys me is people talking in the cinema.
examples.es: Lo que de verdad me molesta es la gente que habla en el cine.

examples.en: It was the music that I loved most.
examples.es: Lo que más me gustó fue la música.

title.en: want / expect / would like + object + to · make / let + object + base form · perfect and passive infinitives and gerunds · verbs + -ing with a change of meaning

summary.es: want / expect / would like + object + to · make / let + object + base form · perfect and passive infinitives and gerunds · verbs + -ing with a change of meaning

explanation.es:
Verbo + objeto + to

Donde el español usa «que + subjuntivo», el inglés usa objeto + to-infinitivo:

I want you to come. (quiero que vengas — ✗ I want that you come)
They expect us to work late. · I'd like him to call me.

make y let

make sb + forma baseobligarShe made me apologise.
let sb + forma basedejar, permitirMy parents let me stay out late.
pasiva: be made to(con to)I was made to apologise.

Formas perfectas y pasivas

to have + participioI'm glad to have met you. He seems to have left.
having + participioShe denied having taken it.
to be + participioI want to be told the truth.
being + participioI hate being interrupted.

Expresiones fijas con -ing

It's no use crying. · It's not worth waiting. · There's no point (in) arguing. · I can't help laughing. · I object to paying more. · She's committed to helping others.
En object to, look forward to, be used to, be committed to, admit to, to es preposición → -ing: ✗ I look forward to hear → ✓ to hearing.

examples.en: My boss wants me to finish the report by Friday.
examples.es: Mi jefe quiere que termine el informe antes del viernes.

examples.en: The teacher made us do the exercise again.
examples.es: El profesor nos hizo repetir el ejercicio.

examples.en: It's not worth waiting for the bus. Let's walk.
examples.es: No merece la pena esperar el autobús. Vamos andando.

examples.en: I hate being told what to do.
examples.es: Odio que me digan lo que tengo que hacer.

examples.en: There's no point in arguing about it.
examples.es: No tiene sentido discutir por eso.

examples.en: He seems to have forgotten our meeting.
examples.es: Parece que se ha olvidado de nuestra reunión.

title.en: hardly any, a great deal of, plenty of, a handful of, the vast majority of · each / every / either / neither · articles with institutions, geography and unique things

summary.es: hardly any, a great deal of, plenty of, a handful of, the vast majority of · each / every / either / neither · articles with institutions, geography and unique things

explanation.es:
Cuantificadores matizados

ContablesIncontablesAmbos
a large number of, numerous, a handful of, a couple of, severala great deal of, a large amount of, a littleplenty of, a lot of, hardly any, no, the majority of (sobre todo contables)
Hardly any students passed. (casi ninguno)
It took a great deal of effort.
The vast majority of people agree.
Only a handful of people came. (un puñado)
each = cada uno por separado; every = todos como grupo (3 o más): Each student has a locker. Every student passed. Los dos con verbo en singular. every two weeks = cada dos semanas.

Artículos en casos difíciles

Sin artículogo to school / church / prison / hospital / university (por su función) · Lake Geneva · Mount Everest · most countries (Spain)
Con thethe school (el edificio) · rivers, seas, oceans (the Thames) · mountain ranges (the Alps) · plural countries (the USA, the Netherlands) · the rich, the elderly
✗ The life is hard → ✓ Life is hard (en general). ✗ the most of people → ✓ most people / most of the people I know.

examples.en: There's hardly any milk left.
examples.es: Casi no queda leche.

examples.en: The project required a great deal of patience.
examples.es: El proyecto requirió muchísima paciencia.

examples.en: Most people think the new law is unfair.
examples.es: La mayoría de la gente piensa que la nueva ley es injusta.

examples.en: She visits her grandmother every two weeks.
examples.es: Visita a su abuela cada dos semanas.

examples.en: Only a handful of people came to the meeting.
examples.es: Solo vino un puñado de personas a la reunión.

examples.en: The vast majority of students passed the exam.
examples.es: La gran mayoría de los alumnos aprobó el examen.

title.en: discourse markers: as far as … is concerned, in terms of, with regard to, by the way, anyway, after all, mind you · formal linkers: whereas, nevertheless, consequently, thus

summary.es: discourse markers: as far as … is concerned, in terms of, with regard to, by the way, anyway, after all, mind you · formal linkers: whereas, nevertheless, consequently, thus

explanation.es:
Organizar las ideas

Introducir un temaAs far as money is concerned, … · In terms of cost, … · With regard to / Regarding your request, …
AñadirBesides, … · What's more, … · Likewise / Similarly, …
ContrastarNevertheless / Nonetheless, … · Conversely, … · whereas / whilst
Consecuencia (formal)Consequently, … · Thus / Hence, …
Concretarnamely (a saber) · notably (en particular)
ResumirTo sum up / Overall / In brief, …

Marcadores de la conversación

Anyway, …bueno, en cualquier caso (volver al tema)
By the way, …por cierto
After all, …al fin y al cabo
Mind you, …eso sí, aunque (matiz)
As a matter of fact / Actually, …de hecho, en realidad
Admittedly, …hay que reconocer que
after all no es «después de todo» en sentido temporal, sino «al fin y al cabo»: Don't be angry with him. After all, he's only six. Para «por fin» usa finally o at last.

title.en: three-part phrasal verbs: come up with, get on with, look up to… · phrasal verbs with particles: up (complete), out (thoroughly), off (start/finish), down (reduce)

summary.es: three-part phrasal verbs: come up with, get on with, look up to… · phrasal verbs with particles: up (complete), out (thoroughly), off (start/finish), down (reduce)

explanation.es:
Phrasal verbs de tres palabras

Verbo + partícula + preposición. Son inseparables: el objeto siempre va al final.

come up withidear, proponerShe came up with a great idea.
put up withaguantarI can't put up with this noise.
catch up with / keep up withalcanzar / seguir el ritmoI can't keep up with the news.
cut down onreducir (consumo)I'm cutting down on sugar.
get away withsalir impuneHe got away with it.
look up to / look down onadmirar / despreciarShe looks up to her grandmother.

En el trabajo

take oncontratar; asumirlay offdespedir (por falta de trabajo)
take overhacerse cargo; absorbercarry outllevar a cabo
step downdimitir, dejar el cargofall throughfracasar, venirse abajo (un plan)
follow uphacer seguimientofill in forsustituir a alguien
point outseñalarsort outsolucionar
Las partículas tienen significados frecuentes: up = completamente (eat up, use up); out = hasta el final, a fondo (work out, sort out); down = reducir (cut down, slow down); on = continuar (carry on, go on).

title.en: prefixes: un-, in-, im-, ir-, il-, dis-, mis-, over-, under-, re-, pre-, co- · suffixes: -ness, -ment, -ity, -tion, -ance, -ful, -less, -ous, -ive, -able, -ise / -ize

summary.es: prefixes: un-, in-, im-, ir-, il-, dis-, mis-, over-, under-, re-, pre-, co- · suffixes: -ness, -ment, -ity, -tion, -ance, -ful, -less, -ous, -ive, -able, -ise / -ize

explanation.es:
Prefijos negativos

un-unhappy, unreliable, unlikely
in- / im- / ir- / il-inaccurate, impossible (ante p, m, b), irresponsible (ante r), illegal (ante l)
dis-dishonest, disagree, disappear
mis- (mal)misunderstand, misspell, mislead

Otros prefijos

over- (demasiado)overcooked, overestimate, oversleepunder- (demasiado poco)underpaid, underestimate
re- (otra vez)rewrite, reconsider, rebuildpre- / post-prehistoric, postgraduate
co- (juntos)co-worker, cooperateex-ex-wife, ex-president

Sufijos

SustantivosAdjetivosVerbos
-ness (happiness), -ment (improvement), -ity (ability), -tion/-sion (explanation), -ance/-ence (appearance, existence), -ship (friendship), -hood (childhood)-ful (useful), -less (careless), -ous (dangerous), -ive (effective), -able/-ible (reliable, flexible), -al (natural), -ic (scientific)-ise/-ize (modernise), -en (widen, shorten), -ify (simplify)
En el examen de la EOI es típica la tarea de «word formation»: mira qué categoría necesita el hueco (sustantivo tras artículo, adjetivo antes de sustantivo, adverbio junto al verbo) y si el sentido es negativo. -ful y -less son opuestos: careful / careless, useful / useless.
✗ unpossible, ✗ inlegal → ✓ impossible, ✓ illegal. ✗ disreliable → ✓ unreliable. Cuidado con los cambios: explain → explanation, pronounce → pronunciation, strong → strength.

title.en: question tags: special cases (Let's…, shall we? / I'm…, aren't I? / Nobody…, did they?) · negative questions · so / neither / nor + auxiliary · I think so / I hope not

summary.es: question tags: special cases (Let's…, shall we? / I'm…, aren't I? / Nobody…, did they?) · negative questions · so / neither / nor + auxiliary · I think so / I hope not

explanation.es:
Question tags: casos especiales

I'm late, aren't I?(no amn't I)
Let's go, shall we?propuesta
Open the window, will you / could you?imperativo
Nobody called, did they?nobody / nothing ya son negativos → tag afirmativo
Everyone was there, weren't they?everyone/somebody → they
There's a problem, isn't there?there is → there
La entonación cambia el sentido: bajando = esperas que te den la razón; subiendo = pregunta real, no estás seguro.

Preguntas negativas

Didn't you hear the alarm? (sorpresa: ¿no oíste…?)
Wouldn't it be better to wait? (sugerencia)
Isn't it beautiful! (exclamación)
Al responder a una pregunta negativa, yes / no se refieren a la realidad, no a la pregunta: — Didn't you go? — No (= no fui) / Yes, I did (= sí fui). El español funciona al revés a menudo, ¡cuidado!

Respuestas cortas y acuerdo

— I love jazz. — So do I.— I can't swim. — Neither / Nor can I.
— Will it rain? — I hope not. / I'm afraid so.— Is she coming? — I think so. / I don't think so.

title.en: idioms · binomials: pros and cons, sooner or later, ups and downs · strong collocations: heavy rain, make a decision, take a risk, pay attention

summary.es: idioms · binomials: pros and cons, sooner or later, ups and downs · strong collocations: heavy rain, make a decision, take a risk, pay attention

explanation.es:
Expresiones idiomáticas

It's a piece of cake.Está chupado.
to break the iceromper el hielo
to cost an arm and a legcostar un ojo de la cara
once in a blue moonde Pascuas a Ramos
to feel under the weatherestar pachucho
It's on the tip of my tongue.Lo tengo en la punta de la lengua.
to hit the nail on the headdar en el clavo
the last strawla gota que colma el vaso
to get cold feetecharse atrás (por miedo)
to call it a daydar por terminado (el día de trabajo)

Binomios (siempre en ese orden)

pros and cons (pros y contras) · sooner or later (tarde o temprano) · ups and downs (altibajos) · by and large (en general) · peace and quiet (tranquilidad) · safe and sound (sano y salvo)

Colocaciones fuertes

adjetivo + sustantivoheavy rain / traffic (✗ strong rain) · strong coffee / wind · high temperature · a close friend
adverbio + adjetivohighly unlikely · bitterly cold · deeply moved · fully aware · widely known
verbo + sustantivotake a risk · pay attention · make an effort · keep a promise · break the law
Los modismos dan naturalidad, pero úsalos con moderación y en registro informal. En una carta formal, It cost an arm and a leg sonaría fuera de lugar.
